headline: Congress cancels EPA's approval of California's stricter nitrogen oxide (NOx) pollution rules for new heavy-duty trucks and diesel engines.
what_it_does: This law uses the Congressional Review Act to cancel an EPA decision that let California set its own, stricter emissions standards. Those standards covered new heavy-duty on-road vehicles and engines from model year 2024 on, plus off-road diesel engines and diesel auxiliary power units. Normally federal law blocks states from setting their own vehicle emission rules unless EPA grants California a waiver. With the waiver revoked, California cannot enforce this "Omnibus" Low NOx rule.

who_it_affects.group: Makers of heavy-duty trucks and engines
who_it_affects.how: They no longer have to meet California's stricter NOx standards for new heavy-duty vehicles and engines sold there.

who_it_affects.group: Makers of off-road diesel engines and auxiliary power units
who_it_affects.how: California's separate standards for these engines covered by the waiver can no longer be enforced.
The state agency loses federal approval to enforce this set of emission rules.

who_it_affects.group: Trucking companies and buyers of heavy-duty vehicles in California
who_it_affects.how: New trucks and engines they buy will not need to meet the California-specific rule covered by the canceled waiver.

who_it_affects.group: Other states that follow California's vehicle standards
who_it_affects.how: States that adopted California's version of these rules may no longer be able to rely on them.
